title: Calloway booking web tier
brief: Calloway Travel needs an architecture page for the booking web tier, owner Booking Platform, region eu-west-1, reviewed 2026-09-28. Under "Overview", two sentences: customers reach us through CloudFront with a WAF in front, and the tier is spread over two Availability Zones to survive losing one. Under "Diagram" show the Booking account, containing the Booking VPC (10.40.0.0/16). Inside the VPC are three groups of subnets: Public subnets (10.40.0.0/23) with the Application Load Balancer and two NAT gateways, "NAT Gateway A" and "NAT Gateway B"; App subnets (10.40.10.0/23) with "Web Fleet A" and "Web Fleet B", each an Auto Scaling group; Data subnets (10.40.20.0/23) with "Bookings DB Primary" and "Bookings DB Standby". An "S3 Gateway Endpoint" also sits in the VPC. Outside the account: Travelers, "CloudFront and WAF" and the "Partner Inventory API". Flows: Travelers to CloudFront and WAF "HTTPS"; CloudFront and WAF to Application Load Balancer "origin request"; Application Load Balancer to Web Fleet A "port 8080"; Application Load Balancer to Web Fleet B "port 8080"; Web Fleet A to Bookings DB Primary "SQL"; Web Fleet B to Bookings DB Primary "SQL"; Bookings DB Primary to Bookings DB Standby "synchronous replication"; Web Fleet A to NAT Gateway A "outbound"; NAT Gateway A to Partner Inventory API "HTTPS"; Web Fleet B to S3 Gateway Endpoint "receipts". Under "Capacity", for each component its size and scaling: Web fleets, m6i.large, 3 to 12 instances per AZ on CPU above 55 percent; Bookings DB, db.r6g.2xlarge Multi-AZ, storage autoscaling to 4 TB; NAT gateways, one per AZ, 5 Gbps each.

edit.request: Change the Bookings DB instance class to db.r6g.4xlarge and add a node called "Redis Session Cache" in the Data subnets, with arrows from Web Fleet A and from Web Fleet B labeled "sessions".
